sources.facts: KPD-RM-04/10, appendix 1 sections 5.1.1.2–5.1.1.5. Three-storey palace and four four-storey corner pavilions, concave hipped roofs, round three-storey east extension with a shallow conical roof, north and south open ground arcades and glazed upper arches, west semi-circular fronton, double ceremonial stairs, shaped cornices, pilasters and rustication.
Palace conservation programme restored the 1692 design, repaired the roof and repaired or restored the elevations, especially the west and south. Restoration culminated in reopening in 2024.
Identifies the park-facing west facade, green corner turrets in historical depiction, and documented second-floor arcaded gallery and leaf-like stucco.
Lithuanian Ministry of Culture identifies the current stand-alone palace and reopening in April 2024 after renovation.
